units.literal: One chief minister should be ordered to compile it.")〉

units.zh: 己卯，吏部侍郎龍敏改尚書左丞。
units.en: On the jimao day, Long Min was transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: On the jimao day, Long Min, Vice Minister of Personnel, was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 己丑，以太子賓客楊凝式為禮部尚書致仕。
units.en: On the jichou day, Yang Ningshi, guest of the heir apparent, was granted retirement as minister of rites.
units.literal: On the jichou day, Yang Ningshi, Guest of the Heir Apparent, was granted retirement as Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 詔建錢爐於欒川。
units.en: An edict ordered coin furnaces built at Luanchuan.
units.literal: An edict ordered coin furnaces built at Luanchuan.

units.zh: 丙申，諫議大夫致仕逍遙先生鄭雲叟卒。
units.en: On the bingshen day, Zheng Yunsou, the retired remonstrance counselor known as Master Xiaoyao, died.
units.literal: On the bingshen day, Zheng Yunsou, retired Remonstrance Counselor and Master Xiaoyao, died.

units.zh: 十二月丁酉朔，百官不入閣，大雪故也。
units.en: On the first day of the twelfth month, the officials did not enter the pavilion because of heavy snow.
units.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, the dingyou day, the hundred officials did not enter the pavilion, because of heavy snow.

units.zh: 己亥，故皇子重英妻張氏落發為尼，賜名悟慎，並夏臘二十。
units.en: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, widow of the late Prince Chongying, took the tonsure as a nun; she was given the name Wushen and twenty summers of monastic age.
units.literal: On the jihai day, Lady Zhang, wife of the late Prince Chongying, shaved her head and became a nun; she was granted the name Wushen and also given twenty summers of monastic age.

units.zh: 庚戌，禮官奏：「來歲正旦，王公上壽，皇帝舉酒，奏《元同之樂》；
units.en: On the gengxu day, the ritual officials submitted: "At New Year's Day next year, when the princes and dukes offer longevity wishes and the emperor raises his cup, the 《Music of Primal Unity》 should be performed;
units.literal: On the gengxu day, the ritual officials submitted: "At New Year's Day next year, when the princes and dukes offer longevity wishes and the Emperor raises his cup, the 《Music of Primal Unity》 should be performed;

units.zh: 再飲，奏《文同之樂》；
units.en: at the second cup, the 《Music of Cultural Unity》;
units.literal: at the second cup, the 《Music of Cultural Unity》;

units.zh: 三飲，奏同前。」
units.en: at the third cup, the same as before."
units.literal: at the third cup, the same as before."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The request was approved.
units.literal: The request was approved.

units.zh: 歌辭不錄。
units.en: The song texts are not recorded.
units.literal: The song texts are not recorded.

units.zh: 丙辰，詔今後城郭村坊，不得創造僧尼院舍。
units.en: On the bingchen day, an edict forbade the construction of new Buddhist monasteries and nunneries in cities, villages, and wards.
units.literal: On the bingchen day, an edict stated that henceforth no new compounds for Buddhist monks or nuns were to be built in walled cities, villages, or wards.

units.zh: 丁巳，帝謂宰臣曰：「大雪害民，五旬未止。
units.en: On the dingsi day, the emperor told the chief ministers, "The heavy snow is harming the people and has not stopped for fifty days.
units.literal: On the dingsi day, the Emperor said to the chief ministers: "The great snow harms the people and has not stopped for fifty days.

units.zh: 京城祠廟，悉令祈禱，了無其驗。
units.en: Temples and shrines throughout the capital have been ordered to pray, yet there has been no effect at all.
units.literal: Temples and shrines in the capital have all been ordered to pray, yet there has been no effect at all.

units.zh: 豈非涼德不儲，神休未洽者乎？」
units.en: Is this not because my meager virtue has not been stored up and divine favor has not been attained?"
units.literal: Is this not because my meager virtue has not been stored up and divine favor has not been attained?"

units.zh: 因令出薪炭米粟給軍士貧民等。
units.en: He therefore ordered fuel, charcoal, rice, and grain distributed to soldiers and the poor.
units.literal: He therefore ordered fuel, charcoal, rice, and grain distributed to soldiers, the poor, and others.

units.zh: 壬戌，禮官奏：「正旦上壽，宮懸歌舞未全，且請雜用九部雅樂，歌教坊法曲。」
units.en: On the renxu day, the ritual officials submitted: "For the New Year's longevity ceremony the palace music and dance are not yet complete; we request for the time being to use selections from the nine bureaus of elegant music and court standard melodies of the Music Office."
units.literal: On the renxu day, the ritual officials submitted: "For the New Year's longevity ceremony, the palace suspended music and dance are not complete; we request for the time being to use mixed selections from the nine bureaus of elegant music and to sing court standard melodies of the Music Office."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The request was approved.
units.literal: The request was approved.

units.zh: 二年二月，刑部尚書盧價奏，纂集《同光刑律統類》凡一十三卷，上之。
units.en: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Justice Lu Jia reported that he had compiled the thirteen-scroll Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes and submitted them to the throne.
units.literal: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Justice Lu Jia memorialized that he had compiled the Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes in thirteen scrolls and presented them.

units.zh: 鄭雲叟，本名遨，雲叟其字也，以唐明宗廟諱，故世傳其字焉，本南燕人也。
units.en: Zheng Yunsou, whose original personal name was Ao and whose courtesy name was Yunsou, was originally a man of Southern Yan. Because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name.
units.literal: Zheng Yunsou, original personal name Ao—Yunsou was his courtesy name; because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name, and he was originally a man of Southern Yan.

units.zh: 嘗因酒酣聯句，鄭曰：「一壺天上有名物，兩個世間無事人。」
units.en: Once, when they were warm with wine, they composed linked verses; Zheng said, "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."
units.literal: Once, when wine had warmed them, they composed linked verses; Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."

units.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，賜近臣傳觀，尋賜號逍遙先生，以諫議大夫致仕，月給俸祿。
units.en: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, having it passed among his close ministers for viewing. He soon granted Yunsou the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.
units.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, ordering it passed among his close ministers for viewing; soon he granted him the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.

units.zh: 唐昭宗朝，嘗應進士舉，不第，因欲攜妻子隱於林壑，其妻非之，不肯行，雲叟乃薄遊諸郡，獲數百緡以贍其家，辭訣而去。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed. He therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys, but his wife disapproved and refused to go. Yunsou then traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.
units.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed; he therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys. His wife disapproved and refused to go, so Yunsou traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.

units.zh: 尋入少室山，著《擬峰詩》三十六章，以導其趣，人多傳之。
units.en: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi and composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, which many people copied and circulated.
units.literal: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi, composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, and many people copied and circulated them.

units.zh: 俄聞西嶽有五鬛松，淪脂千年，能去三屍，因居於華陰。
units.en: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses, and he therefore settled at Huayin.
units.literal: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses; he therefore settled at Huayin.

units.zh: 少好學，耿介不屈。
units.en: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.
units.literal: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.

units.zh: 與羅隱之朝夕遊處，隱之以藥術取利，雲叟以山田自給，俱好酒能詩，善長嘯。
units.en: He spent his days with Luo Yinzhi, who made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from hillside fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry well, and were skilled at long whistling.
units.literal: He spent his days and nights in company with Luo Yinzhi; Yinzhi made a living through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself with hillside fields. Both loved wine and were skilled at poetry, and excelled at long whistling.

units.zh: 雲叟好酒，嘗為《詠酒詩》千二百言，海內好名者書於縑緗，以為贈貺。
units.en: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters. Admirers throughout the realm copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.
units.literal: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters; those throughout the realm who admired his name copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.

units.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。
units.en: His collected works in twenty juan circulated widely.
units.literal: A collection of writings in twenty juan circulated in the world.

units.zh: 後妻兒繼謝，每聞兇服，一哭而止。
units.en: Later his wife and children died one after another; whenever he heard that someone was in mourning, he wept once and stopped.
units.literal: Later his wife and children died in succession; whenever he heard of mourning garments, he wept once and stopped.

units.zh: 後妻以書達意，勸其還家，雲叟未嘗一覽，悉投於火，其絕累如此。
units.en: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home, but Yunsou never so much as read it—he threw it all into the fire. Such was his severing of worldly ties.
units.literal: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home; Yunsou never so much as read it once—he threw it all into the fire. So thorough was his severing of worldly ties.

units.zh: 與李道殷、羅隱之友善，時人目為「三高士」。
units.en: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
units.literal: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi; people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."

units.zh: 道殷有釣魚之術，鉤而不餌，又能化易金石，無所不至，雲叟恒目睹其事，信而不求。
units.en: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.
units.literal: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait, and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.

units.zh: 雲叟與梁室權臣李振善，振欲祿之，拒而不諾，及振南遷，雲叟千里徒步以省之，識者高焉。
units.en: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court. Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but Yunsou refused. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him, and those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.
units.literal: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court; Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but he refused and would not agree. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him—those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.

units.zh: 時惟青衿二童子、一琴、一鶴，從其遊處。
units.en: At that time only two youths in blue collars, a zither, and a crane accompanied him wherever he went.
units.literal: At that time only two youths in blue collars, one zither, and one crane accompanied him in his wanderings.

units.zh: 好棋塞之戲，遇同侶則以晝繼夜，雖寒風大雪，臨檐對局，手足皸裂，亦無倦焉。
units.en: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss; when he found companions he would play from day into night. Even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves across the board from them with cracked hands and feet, he never grew weary.
units.literal: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss games; when he met companions he would continue from day into night, and even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves facing one another across the board, his hands and feet cracked with chilblains, yet he never showed weariness.

units.zh: 唐天成中，召拜左拾遺，不起。
units.en: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Aide but declined to serve.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrance Aide but did not take up the post.

units.zh: 有大瓠，雲可辟寒暑，置酒於其中，經時味不壞，日攜就花木水石之間，一酌一詠。
units.en: He owned a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; wine placed in it did not spoil even after a long time. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, drinking and composing a verse in turn.
units.literal: He had a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; he placed wine in it and even after a long time the flavor did not spoil. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, taking a drink and composing a verse.

units.zh: 高祖即位，聞其名，遣使賫書致禮，征為右諫議大夫，雲叟稱疾不起，上表陳謝。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he heard of Yunsou's fame and sent an envoy with a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master. Yunsou pleaded illness and declined, submitting a memorial of thanks.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he heard of Yunsou's name and sent an envoy bearing a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master; Yunsou pleaded illness and did not rise, submitting a memorial to decline with thanks.

units.zh: 復有越千里之外，使畫工潛寫其形容列為屏障者焉。
units.en: Some even from beyond a thousand li sent painters to sketch his likeness in secret and mount it on screens.
units.literal: There were also those from more than a thousand li away who sent painters to sketch his likeness secretly and array it on screens.

units.zh: 其為時望所重也如此。
units.en: Such was the esteem his contemporaries accorded him.
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.

units.zh: 天福末，以壽終，時年七十四。
units.en: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at the age of seventy-four.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at age seventy-four.

units.zh: 唯玉羽之貞退，雲叟之肥遁，足可以柅奔競之風，激高尚之節也。
units.en: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were enough to check the wind of frantic striving and inspire the integrity of the lofty-minded.
units.literal: Only Yuyu's steadfast withdrawal and Yunsou's ample reclusion were sufficient to check the wind of frantic striving and inspire the integrity of the lofty-minded.

units.zh: 羅曰：「醉卻隱之、雲叟外，不知何處是天真。」
units.en: Luo said, "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
units.literal: Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."

units.zh: 吳承範，字表微，魏州人也。
units.en: Wu Chengfan, courtesy name Biaowei, was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Wu Chengfan, style name Biaowei, was a man of Weizhou.

units.zh: 承範溫厚寡言，善希人旨，桑維翰、李崧尤重之，嘗薦於高祖，雲可大用。
units.en: Wu Chengfan was gentle and sparing of words, adept at reading others' wishes. Sang Weihan and Li Song held him in special regard and once recommended him to Gaozu as fit for high office.
units.literal: Chengfan was mild and reticent, skilled at discerning others' intent. Sang Weihan and Li Song especially valued him and once recommended him to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.

units.zh: 承範少好學，善屬文，唐閔帝之鎮鄴都也，聞其才名，署為賓職，承範懇求隨計，閔帝許之。
units.en: From youth Chengfan loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was stationed at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly asked to accompany him on the tribute journey to the capital, and Emperor Min agreed.
units.literal: Chengfan from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was posted at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly requested to accompany him on the tribute journey, and Emperor Min permitted it.

units.zh: 承範知之，持重自養，雖遇盛夏，而猶服襦袴，加之以純綿，蓋慮有寒濕之患也。
units.en: Chengfan understood this and kept himself in careful reserve. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers lined with cotton, lest he suffer from cold and damp.
units.literal: Chengfan knew this and cultivated himself with restraint. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers with pure cotton added, fearing ailments from cold and damp.

units.zh: 及閔帝即位，授左拾遺。
units.en: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.
units.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.

units.zh: 清泰二年，以本官充史館修撰，與同職張昭遠等共修《明宗實錄》，轉右補闕，依前充職。
units.en: In the second year of Qingtai, while retaining his existing post he was made compiler at the Historiography Institute and, together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in the same office.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai, in his existing capacity he was made Compiler at the Historiography Institute and together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in his former office.

units.zh: 高祖革命，遷尚書屯田員外郎、知制誥。
units.en: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, he was promoted to vice director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
units.literal: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and Drafter of Edicts.

units.zh: 天福三年，改樞密院直學士，未幾，自祠部郎中、知制誥召充翰林學士，正拜中書舍人，賜金紫。
units.en: In the third year of Tianfu he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Secretariat drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianfu he was changed to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafter of Edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，遷禮部侍郎，知貢舉，尋遘疾而卒，年四十二。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was promoted to vice minister of rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died at the age of forty-two.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died, aged forty-two.

units.zh: 長興三年春，擢進士第。
units.en: In spring of the third year of Changxing he passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: In spring of the third year of Changxing, he was selected as a jinshi.

units.zh: 父瓊，右金吾衛將軍，累贈太子少保。
units.en: His father Qiong was general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was posthumously honored on successive occasions as junior guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: His father Qiong was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was repeatedly posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 贈工部尚書。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as minister of works.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.

units.zh: 然竟不獲其志，其命也夫！
units.en: Yet in the end he never attained his ambition—such was fate!
units.literal: Yet in the end he did not realize his ambition—such was his fate!

units.zh: 晉高祖時，詔天下求孝悌之士，戶部尚書王權、宗正卿石光贊、國子祭酒田敏、兵部侍郎王延等相與詣東上閤門，上昂行義可以應詔。
units.en: Under Gaozu of Jin, the court sought filial and dutiful men across the realm. Wang Quan, Minister of Revenue; Shi Guangzan, Director of the Imperial Clan Court; Tian Min, Director of the National University; Wang Yan, Vice Minister of War; and others went together to the Eastern Upper Gate and recommended Ang’s conduct as meeting the edict.
units.literal: Under Gaozu of Jin, an edict sought filial and brotherly men throughout the realm. Minister of Revenue Wang Quan, Director of the Imperial Clan Court Shi Guangzan, Director of the National University Tian Min, Vice Minister of War Wang Yan, and others together went to the Eastern Upper Gate of the Secretariat and memorialized that Ang’s conduct and righteousness qualified him to answer the edict.
